s: Among the exiles by the river Chebar, Ezekiel sees the glory of God: living creatures, wheels and a throne.
God sends Ezekiel to a rebellious people.
Ezekiel eats the scroll and is made a watchman for Israel.
Ezekiel acts out the siege of Jerusalem with a brick and lies on his side.
Ezekiel shaves his head and divides the hair, a sign of what will happen to Jerusalem.
Prophecy against the mountains of Israel and their idols.
The end has come upon the land.
In a vision Ezekiel sees idol worship in the temple.
The faithful are marked on the forehead, and the idolaters are struck down.
God's glory rises from the temple.
God promises a new heart and a new spirit. His glory leaves the city.
Ezekiel packs his baggage as a sign of the coming exile.
Against false prophets who say peace when there is no peace.
Even Noah, Daniel and Job could not save the land by their goodness.
Jerusalem is a useless vine, fit only to burn.
Jerusalem is like an unfaithful bride, yet God will remember his covenant.
The parable of two eagles and a vine. God will plant a tender shoot on a high mountain.
Each person is responsible for his own sin. God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked: turn and live.
A lament for the princes of Israel.
God recalls Israel's rebellions and promises to gather them again.
The sword of the Lord is drawn against Jerusalem.
Jerusalem's sins and the furnace of judgment.
The two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah, stand for Samaria and Jerusalem.
The siege begins. Ezekiel's wife dies, and he is told not to mourn, as a sign.
Prophecies against Ammon, Moab, Edom and the Philistines.
Prophecy against Tyre.
A lament for Tyre, the great trading ship.
Against the prince of Tyre. Prophecy against Sidon.
Prophecy against Egypt.
Egypt's day of judgment.
Pharaoh compared to a great cedar that is cut down.
A lament for Pharaoh and Egypt.
Ezekiel the watchman. News comes that Jerusalem has fallen.
Against the false shepherds of Israel. God himself will shepherd his sheep.
Prophecy against Mount Seir.
God will give a new heart and put his Spirit within his people.
The valley of dry bones comes to life. The two sticks of Israel and Judah become one.
Prophecy against Gog.
Gog's defeat. God will pour out his Spirit on Israel.
A vision of the new temple: the gates and courts.
The temple and its rooms are measured.
The priests' rooms and the outer wall.
The glory of the Lord returns to the temple.
Rules for the priests in the new temple.
The holy portion of land and the offerings.
The worship of the prince and the people.
A river flows from the temple and brings life wherever it goes.
The land is divided among the tribes. The city's name will be: The Lord is there.

36: A new heart and a new spirit
God promises to wash his people clean and put his own Spirit within them, a promise fulfilled in baptism and Pentecost.
37: God brings dead bones to life by his Spirit, a sign that he can raise his people from death.
